about: The psalm begins in the middle — at verse 6 — because that is the verse that names the altar: I will wash my hands and go about thy altar. What the priest washes is not his whole hands but the tips of the thumbs and index fingers: the ones that will touch the consecrated host. The psalm speaks of innocence, and speaks it in the first person — “I have walked in my innocence” — which at the altar sounds like a petition rather than a boast: “rédime me”, redeem me, follows two lines later. The Glória Patri is omitted in Masses for the Dead and from Passion Sunday to Holy Thursday inclusive; the psalm itself stays.

s01.narrative: The priest moves to the right side of the altar; the server pours water over his fingertips.

s02.translation: I will wash my hands among the innocent, and go about thy altar, Lord:

s03.translation: That I may hear the voice of praise, and tell all thy wonders.

s04.translation: Lord, I have loved the beauty of thy house, and the place of the dwelling of thy glory.

s05.translation: Destroy not my soul with the wicked, God, nor my life with men of blood:

s06.translation: In whose hands are iniquities: their right hand is filled with gifts.

s07.translation: But I have walked in my innocence: redeem me, and have mercy on me.

s08.translation: My foot hath stood in the straight way: in the assemblies I will bless thee, Lord.

s09.translation: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

s10.translation: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, unto ages of ages. Amen.

w001.function: A future opens the psalm and sets the tense for the three main verbs that follow.

w003.function: An adjective standing as a noun. In-nocens: one who does no harm.

w004.function: One spelling serving six slots of the paradigm; accusative plural here, because it is the object of “Lavábo” (w001).

w007.function: The stress falls on the antepenult, because the a of dare is short; some editions accent it otherwise.

w011.function: It opens a purpose clause: what the washing and the circling are for.

w012.function: The form is also a future; the subjunctive is settled by “enárrem” (w016), which can be nothing else.

w016.function: E-narráre: to recount in order, to tell through to the end.

w018.function: A neuter plural adjective standing as a noun: the things worth wondering at.

w021.function: Dilígere is love by choice — literally to pick out from among; not feeling but preference.

w023.function: Genitive singular; the same spelling serves the nominative and the plural, and dependence on “decórem” (w022) decides.

w028.function: Two genitives one after another: the place of the dwelling — of what? — of thy glory.

w030.function: A prohibition or negative petition takes ne in Latin, not non.

w031.function: Subjunctive in a negative petition: do not destroy.

w033.function: An adjective standing as a noun, like “innocéntes” (w003) at the psalm's opening — the two sides the psalmist asks to be sorted between.

w040.function: A genitive plural: literally “men of bloods”. A Hebrew way of naming murderers, rendered word for word.

w042.function: Soul and life stand in parallel — one thing said twice over, as Hebrew poetry says it.

w044.function: It refers back to “viris” (w039) in the verse before — the psalm goes on about the same men.

w045.function: The same hands as in the first verse, but another's, and full of something else.

w051.function: With “repléta” (w050) it makes one past passive form; on its own it means nothing here.

w052.function: Ablative of means. Munus is a gift, but also a due paid — here a bribe.

w053.function: The pronoun is written out because it contrasts: they so — I otherwise.

w059.function: With “ingréssus” (w058) it makes one perfect form of a deponent verb; on its own it means nothing here.

w060.function: Red-émere: to buy back, to ransom a captive. The petition, set right after the claim of innocence, takes the boast out of it.

w064.function: The genitive of the pronoun “I”, not the possessive “my”: misereor governs the genitive of the person pitied.

w069.function: A neuter standing as a noun: “in what is straight”. The image is of a road, not of posture.

w071.function: Ecclésia is first of all a gathering summoned; the sense of a church building is later.

w072.function: The form would also allow a subjunctive; the future rests on the main clause and on the company of “Lavábo” (w001).

w075.function: A verbless sentence: “glory to the Father” — “be” is understood.
